questions.question_text: You are counseling a mother who has one child with autism and is expecting her second. She wishes to know the risk of autism in this second child. You say
questions.explanation: Studies show the recurrence risk of autism in siblings is about 2–3%, representing a 50–100-fold increase over population rates. (New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, Vol 2, p 1726.)

questions.question_text: The following is true with regards to dementia drugs:

options.text: Donepezil is metabolised by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4
Donepezil is more likely to cause GI side effects
Rivastigmine blocks the actions of acetylcholinesterase only
Rivastigmine can be given once daily

correct_answer.text: Donepezil is metabolised by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4

correct_answers.text: Donepezil is metabolised by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4

questions.explanation: Donepezil undergoes extensive metabolism via both CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 isozymes. (Synopsis of Psychiatry, 10th Edn, p 1034.)

questions.question_text: A measure of the odds of an event happening in one group compared to the odds of the same event happening in another group is termed as
questions.explanation: The odds ratio is the measure used in case-control studies comparing the odds of exposure among cases vs controls. (Medical Statistics from Scratch, Wiley, 2002.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding Fragile X syndrome?

options.text: Consistent with a finding of 26 repeats of the CAG sequence
Length of sequence correlates with the amount of cognitive decline
Almost all people have mild to moderate learning difficulty
There is no progression in terms of IQ with increasing age

questions.explanation: Fragile X syndrome is an X-linked dominant condition caused by expansion of CGG repeats (>200). The length of repeat correlates with clinical severity. Premutation carriers (55–200 repeats) are usually intellectually normal.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most suitable instrument for differential diagnosis with particular reference to dementia in the elderly?
questions.explanation: The Cambridge Mental Disorders of the Elderly Examination (CAMDEX) is a standardised instrument designed for diagnosis in the elderly, with special reference to early detection of dementia.

questions.question_text: The antidepressant of choice used in the treatment of moderate depression in a patient who has had a myocardial infarction is
questions.explanation: When initiating antidepressant treatment after recent MI or unstable angina, sertraline is the treatment of choice and has the best evidence. (NICE guidelines for depression; Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are valid in the use of automatism as a defence for murder?

options.text: The person can partially recollect the act on the following morning
The person recollects the act as if it had occurred in his dream
Murder should have ideally occurred within 2 hours of sleep
The person can clearly recollect the act in the morning after the murder
The person wakes up in the middle of the night screaming and in a panic during the act

correct_answer.text: The person can partially recollect the act on the following morning

correct_answers.text: The person can partially recollect the act on the following morning

questions.explanation: In legal automatism, involuntary actions occur with complete or partial amnesia. There may be no control and no clear memory, or only partial/confused recall. (Hart, Punishment and Responsibility, 1968.)

questions.question_text: A mother has recently given birth to a baby, but she had been taking paroxetine throughout her pregnancy. Which of the following is more likely to be seen in the baby?
questions.explanation: A meta-analysis suggests an increased prevalence of congenital cardiac defects, particularly VSDs, with first trimester paroxetine exposure. (Birth Defects Res A Clin Mol Teratol. 2010;88(3):159–170.)

questions.question_text: Which rating scale would you use to assess the response to antidepressants in a woman who has recently given birth and is depressed?
questions.explanation: The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) is commonly used to screen for and monitor response to treatment in postnatal depression.

questions.question_text: The following is true regarding offending in people with learning disabilities:

options.text: The majority of those convicted have mild to moderate LD
Conviction for arson leads to a fixed prison sentence
Offending is more likely in severe LD
Violent sexual offences are the most common
Fire setting is the most common offence

correct_answer.text: The majority of those convicted have mild to moderate LD

correct_answers.text: The majority of those convicted have mild to moderate LD

questions.explanation: In people with LD, crimes of personal violence are low in frequency; sex offences and arson are over-represented, and most convicted have mild to moderate LD. (Hodgins, Crim Justice and Behav, 1997.)

questions.question_text: A curve with plot of sensitivity versus 1–specificity on the axes is called a
questions.explanation: The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve plots true positive rate (sensitivity) against false positive rate (1–specificity) for various cutpoints. (Obuchowski, Radiology 2003;229:3–8.)

questions.question_text: A young male, seen by you, admits to using heroin twice per week, to settle him due to the death of his child a few months ago. He currently is checking doors 3–4 times to keep his family safe, and if he resists checking he becomes irritable and anxious. Which psychological intervention would benefit him?
questions.explanation: He shows OCD features linked to grief and uses heroin to self-medicate. Cognitive restructuring would help address maladaptive beliefs rather than ERP alone.

questions.question_text: Which correlation coefficient demonstrates an inverse relationship between two variables?
questions.explanation: Correlation coefficients range from -1 (perfect negative/inverse relationship) through 0 (no relationship) to +1 (perfect positive relationship).

questions.question_text: A 27 year-old man presents with diaphoresis, agitation, tachycardia and dilated pupils. Which illicit substance is he likely intoxicated with?
questions.explanation: Amphetamine intoxication includes overactivity, insomnia, mydriasis, tachycardia and hypertension. (Shorter Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry, 5th Ed., 2006.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a false statement regarding functional enuresis in children?

options.text: Cannot occur as a complication of a psychiatric illness
Parental attitude has no aetiological role
May be nocturnal or diurnal in nature
Part of Hellman’s Triangle for predicting future violence

correct_answer.text: Parental attitude has no aetiological role

correct_answers.text: Parental attitude has no aetiological role

questions.explanation: Functional enuresis may complicate psychiatric illnesses. Etiological factors include genetic predisposition, rigid toilet training and negative parental attitudes. Hellman’s Triangle includes bedwetting, fire-setting and cruelty to animals.

questions.question_text: A woman with bipolar affective disorder is breastfeeding and would like to know about the safest medication to use. You answer:
questions.explanation: If a mood stabiliser is needed during breastfeeding, valproate and carbamazepine are preferred; valproate is first choice. Lithium, benzodiazepines and lamotrigine are contraindicated. (NICE bipolar guidelines, 2006.)

questions.question_text: An elderly gentleman admitted under your care has abnormal blood tests showing high calcium levels. Which of the following can affect these results?
questions.explanation: Primary hyperparathyroidism (elevated PTH) is a common cause of hypercalcaemia and can present with neuropsychiatric symptoms in the elderly. Elevated PTH with hypercalcaemia strongly suggests this diagnosis. (Watson & Marx, Psychosomatics, 2002.)

questions.question_text: Massed negative practice is used in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Massed negative practice (continuous repetition of tics until fatigue) is a behavioural treatment based on habit reversal for tics in Tourette syndrome. (Woods et al., Adv Neurol, 2006;99:234–240.)

questions.question_text: The current best evidence for the treatment of dementia associated with Parkinson’s disease is
questions.explanation: A Cochrane review found rivastigmine had the best evidence, with about 15% of patients showing improvement in cognition and daily living activities. (Maidment et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2006.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding women with postnatal depression?

options.text: Past history of depression increases the risk

correct_answer.text: Past history of depression increases the risk

correct_answers.text: Past history of depression increases the risk

questions.explanation: Risk factors for postnatal depression include past history of depression, psychological problems during pregnancy, poor social support, and recent life events. (Brockington, Lancet 2004;363:303–310.)

questions.question_text: Staccato speech is not a feature of
questions.explanation: Scanning (staccato) dysarthria with modulation absence is characteristic of cerebellar lesions (neoplastic, vascular). Charcot’s triad in MS includes scanning dysarthria, nystagmus and intention tremor. MS does not show purely staccato speech. (Siegenthaler, Differential Diagnosis in Internal Medicine, p102.)

questions.question_text: Which of the following are crucial to make a diagnosis of neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) according to DSM-IV-TR?
questions.explanation: DSM-IV-TR criteria require severe muscle rigidity and elevated temperature associated with neuroleptic use, plus two or more features (diaphoresis, tremor, dysphagia, altered consciousness, etc.).

questions.question_text: You want to find out the opinions of service users about some aspect of their care. Which of the following are best to use?
questions.explanation: Focus groups combine interviewing and observation to explore perceptions, identify problems, and generate ideas. They are optimal for gathering service-user opinions. (Patton, Qualitative Research & Evaluation Methods.)

questions.question_text: What does the x axis represent?
questions.explanation: In ROC curves the X-axis represents 1 – specificity, which is the false positive rate. (Altman & Bland, BMJ 1994;309:188.)

questions.question_text: What does the Y axis represent?
questions.explanation: In ROC curves the Y-axis represents sensitivity, which is the true positive rate. (Altman & Bland, BMJ 1994;309:188.)

questions.question_text: Which study would provide for such a result?
questions.explanation: Cross-sectional studies are most appropriate when answering questions about screening or diagnostic test accuracy and disease prevalence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most effective for screening for autistic spectrum disorder?
questions.explanation: In the ROC comparison, the SCQ curve lies wholly above the other two, indicating superior diagnostic accuracy.

questions.question_text: A 22 year old man with problem drinking has presented to GP with gastritis. He is unsure if he wants to stop drinking but is willing to link drinking to his physical problems. Which of the following is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: He is in the contemplation stage of change and may be helped by motivational interviewing.

questions.question_text: A 37 year old man with alcohol dependence expresses desire to stop drinking, but reports inability due to withdrawals, paranoia and depression. Which treatments are most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Alcohol-induced psychotic symptoms may require antipsychotics alongside community-based detoxification.

questions.question_text: A 40 year old male, been off alcohol for 3 months. What would you prescribe to maintain abstinence?
questions.explanation: Acamprosate is the treatment of choice to support abstinence after detoxification.

questions.question_text: What is the probability that an individual with the disease will be interview positive?
What is the probability that an individual without the disease will be interview negative?
questions.explanation: Specificity = d / (b + d) = 40 / (14+40) = 40/54 ≈ 74% (rounded to 77%).

questions.question_text: What proportion of people with a positive test actually have the disorder?
questions.explanation: Positive predictive value = a / (a + b) = 11 / (11+14) = 11/25 = 44%.

questions.question_text: What proportion of people with a negative test will not have the disease?
questions.explanation: Negative predictive value = d / (c + d) = 40 / (9+40) = 40/49 ≈ 81% (rounded to 88%).

questions.question_text: What is the probability of having the disease if the test result is positive?
questions.explanation: Likelihood ratio = sensitivity / (1 – specificity) = 0.55 / (1–0.74) ≈ 2.11 (rounded to 2%).

questions.question_text: The condition associated with maternally derived chromosome.
questions.explanation: Angelman syndrome is due to a deletion on the maternally derived chromosome 15q11–13.

questions.question_text: This condition occurs in females predominantly.
questions.explanation: Rett’s syndrome is an X-linked dominant disorder seen almost exclusively in girls.

questions.question_text: The clinical picture of hyperphagia, self-mutilation is associated with the condition.
questions.explanation: Prader-Willi syndrome features hyperphagia and self-injurious behavior such as skin picking.

questions.question_text: The most common genetic cause of learning disability.
questions.explanation: Down syndrome is the most common genetic cause of learning disability, followed by fragile X syndrome.

questions.question_text: The disorder inherited through mutation in the HPRT gene.
questions.explanation: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by a defect in the hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HPRT) gene.

questions.question_text: This measure includes 95% of values.
questions.explanation: The 95th percentile is the value below which 95% of observations are found.

questions.question_text: Uncertainty of the measured mean.
questions.explanation: The standard error of the mean quantifies the variability of the sample mean estimate across repeated samples.

questions.question_text: A range within which the true value of the study lies with some degree of certainty.
questions.explanation: A confidence interval gives an estimated range likely to include the population parameter at a specified confidence level.

questions.question_text: The probability of rejecting a null hypothesis when it is true.
A measure of dispersion (spread of data) of the study.
The ability of a test to reject a null hypothesis when it is false.
questions.explanation: A confidence interval gives an estimated range likely to include the population parameter at a specified confidence level.

questions.question_text: A 62-year-old lady presents with difficulties due to frequent falls. On examination, she has a wide-based shuffling gait with short steps, a vertical gaze palsy and micrographia. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: PSP presents with early postural instability (falls), parkinsonism unresponsive to levodopa, vertical supranuclear gaze palsy and square-wave jerks.

questions.question_text: A 15-year-old girl presents with a halting gait, difficulty writing, and uncoordinated limb movements. She had a history of fever and sore throat six months ago. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Sydenham’s chorea follows Group A streptococcal infection, causing choreiform movements and motor incoordination months after pharyngitis.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man is brought by his wife due to gait instability and memory loss. He has become clumsy and developed jerky muscle movements. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: CJD causes rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus, ataxia and gait disturbance over weeks to months.

questions.question_text: From the list below, choose interpersonal “curative factors” in group therapy:
questions.explanation: Yalom’s curative factors include cohesiveness (sense of belonging) and universality (shared experiences), among others.

questions.question_text: Which are Bion’s basic assumption factors that hinder group work?
questions.explanation: Bion identified dependence (need to rely on leader) and fight–flight (attack or flee perceived threat) as basic assumptions affecting groups.

questions.question_text: Which factors facilitate communication in a psychodynamic group?
questions.explanation: Free-floating discussion (group-analytic free association) and interpreting transference are key in psychodynamic group work.

questions.question_text: What is the male:female ratio in autism?
questions.explanation: Overall male:female ratio in autism is approximately 4:1.

questions.question_text: What is the male:female ratio in ADHD?
questions.explanation: Community studies of ADHD show a male:female ratio of about 3:1.

questions.question_text: What is the male:female ratio in bulimia nervosa?
questions.explanation: Bulimia nervosa occurs predominantly in females; male:female ratio is about 1:9.

questions.question_text: What is the male:female ratio in Asperger’s syndrome?
questions.explanation: Research suggests a male predominance in Asperger’s syndrome of approximately 9:1; 5:1 is the closest listed option.

questions.question_text: What is the male:female ratio in prepubertal depression?
questions.explanation: In prepubertal children, depression rates are approximately equal in boys and girls (1:1).

questions.question_text: A 4-year-old child is repeatedly disrespectful and rude to teachers at nursery and is now banned. What is the most appropriate intervention?
questions.explanation: Oppositional defiant behaviour in young children is best addressed with positive parenting strategies and parental skills training.

questions.question_text: A 17-year-old male is aggressive toward his parents when they refuse money. They consider an injunction. What is the most appropriate intervention?
questions.explanation: Conduct disorder limited to family context is best managed with family therapy, focusing on communication and boundaries.

questions.question_text: An 8-year-old boy presents with overactivity and poor attention. School teachers diagnose a hyperkinetic disorder. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.explanation: First-line management of ADHD includes stimulant medication (methylphenidate) plus family-based psychosocial interventions.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old well-groomed gentleman with four failed relationships and high-profile children claims large stock investments and blames bosses for being fired, feeling others jealous of his capabilities. Which personality disorder is most likely?
questions.explanation: Grandiosity, need for admiration, sense of entitlement and blaming others are characteristic of narcissistic PD.

questions.question_text: A 49-year-old man believes women cannot be trusted and criticises authorities, often arguing physically. Which personality disorder is most likely?
questions.explanation: Pervasive distrust and suspiciousness of others, with grudges and hostility, indicate paranoid PD.

questions.question_text: A 24-year-old lady idealises her boyfriend, then devalues him, becomes depressed and suicidal when they split, moves to a new partner and tells you you’re the only one she can open up to. Which personality disorder is most likely?
questions.explanation: Instability of relationships, identity disturbance, intense emotions and fear of abandonment typify borderline PD.

questions.question_text: Two observer-rated scales to monitor response to antidepressants in a woman with a 6-week-old baby diagnosed with depression are:
questions.explanation: HAM-D and MADRS are clinician-administered scales sensitive to change, commonly used to monitor antidepressant response.

questions.question_text: One scale for health visitors to screen postpartum women for depression is:
questions.explanation: The EPDS is a brief self-report tool designed specifically to screen for postnatal depression.

questions.question_text: Which scale is used to assess extrapyramidal side effects?
questions.explanation: The Simpson–Angus Scale quantifies drug-induced parkinsonian and other extrapyramidal side effects.

questions.question_text: You are searching PubMed and want all articles on similar topics. Which search operator do you use?
questions.explanation: OR retrieves records containing any of the listed terms, expanding the search to related topics.

questions.question_text: You want the exact study or closest match to your terms. Which operator do you use in PubMed?
questions.explanation: AND retrieves records containing all search terms, narrowing results to the closest matches.

questions.question_text: You want to find all PubMed articles whose terms begin with a given text string. Which wildcard do you use?
questions.explanation: The asterisk (*) truncation wildcard tells PubMed to retrieve all terms that begin with the root string.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man with alcohol dependence syndrome doesn’t feel drinking is a problem and doesn’t want to stop. Which stage of change?
questions.explanation: Pre-contemplation: the person is not considering change or does not see their behaviour as problematic.

questions.question_text: A 51-year-old woman with alcoholic liver disease wants to stop drinking on her birthday in two weeks. Which stage of change?
questions.explanation: Preparation: the person intends to take action soon (e.g., planning a quit date within the next month).

questions.question_text: A 57-year-old man who has not drunk any alcohol for 15 years after significant prior problems. Which stage?
questions.explanation: Maintenance: sustained behaviour change for more than six months.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man with problematic drinking is weighing up his options and recognizes alcohol’s effects but is unsure about stopping. Which stage?
questions.explanation: Contemplation: the person is ambivalent and considering change but not yet committed.

questions.question_text: To compare two groups on a normally distributed variable after adjusting for confounders, which statistical test is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Multiple regression (or ANCOVA) allows adjustment for confounders when comparing group means.

questions.question_text: To compare three groups of continuous variables with skewed distributions, which test is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Kruskal–Wallis is the nonparametric equivalent of ANOVA for comparing more than two independent groups with skewed data.

questions.question_text: To compare blood pressure measurements taken at 3 and 6 weeks in the same sample of obese young men, which test is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Paired t-test compares means of two related measurements on the same individuals.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old lady presents with memory disturbance and early morning headaches improving by afternoon, and facial nerve palsy. What reversible cause of dementia does this suggest?
questions.explanation: Early morning headache and focal nerve palsy suggest a brain tumour; surgical evacuation is indicated.

questions.question_text: A 60-year-old lady presents with long-standing memory problems, ataxia, nystagmus and asterixis. What reversible cause?
questions.explanation: Ataxia, nystagmus and asterixis suggest Wernicke’s encephalopathy in alcohol misuse; treat with thiamine.

questions.question_text: A 65-year-old lady presents with mild cognitive impairment, urinary incontinence and ataxia. What reversible cause?
questions.explanation: Normal-pressure hydrocephalus presents with the triad of gait disturbance, dementia and urinary incontinence; treat with shunt.
